latency_playbook.parallelization: fan out SQL-only and graph-lookup validations across a thread pool before any LLM call
latency_playbook.expected_gain: Avoid remote warehouse latency for the common case; ideal for analytics, hierarchy, and timeline questions.

latency_playbook.parallelization: cache evidence bundles by question_id + corpus + db snapshot so repeated rubric passes only touch changed questions
latency_playbook.expected_gain: Prevents re-querying the same email threads, org rows, and verse bundles during iterative curation.

latency_playbook.parallelization: run sql_only and graph_lookup batches at higher concurrency; keep judge-heavy synthesis batches smaller
latency_playbook.expected_gain: Maximizes throughput without overloading the expensive LLM-judge path.

latency_playbook.parallelization: only send questions to LLM judges after answerability/evidence prechecks pass
latency_playbook.expected_gain: Cuts avoidable LLM calls and shortens the tail latency of the curation loop.

latency_playbook.parallelization: generate candidates independently per weak slice rather than serially across the whole bank
latency_playbook.expected_gain: Lets AVL target multiple empty or thin slices in parallel without coupling unrelated domains.

latency_playbook.parallelization: stop when no new validated promotions or meaningful coverage gains appear over recent cycles
latency_playbook.expected_gain: Avoids wasting cycles on candidate churn once the curation frontier stops moving.
